title: Divorce under Special Marriage Act — Section 27 SMA

content.overview: Section 27 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides contested divorce grounds for a marriage solemnised or registered under the Act, including adultery, desertion, imprisonment, cruelty, and specified mental-disorder grounds, together with additional wife-specific and post-decree grounds as enacted.
content.glance: Ask: (1) SMA marriage? (2) Which s. 27 ground? (3) Ingredients proved? (4) Not mutual-consent path (s. 28)?
content.study:
Do not cite HMA s. 13 grounds by number for an SMA marriage; use s. 27 of the SMA.

Case already in migrated file: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511 — mental cruelty is fact-sensitive; illustrative categories; statutory ground must be proved on the facts. No additional cases invented.

sections.heading: Contested grounds
sections.body: Adultery, desertion, imprisonment, cruelty, mental-disorder grounds and other heads as in s. 27.

sections.heading: Wife-specific / post-decree grounds
sections.body: Additional grounds as enacted in the section for the wife and after certain decrees.

sections.heading: Proof
sections.body: Each ground must be proved on the facts; cruelty is fact-sensitive.

sections.heading: Contrast with s. 28
sections.body: s. 27 is contested; s. 28 is mutual consent.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: District Court / Family Court as applicable under the Act and Family Courts Act.

examples.title: Cruelty petition
examples.body: Spouse petitions under s. 27 on cruelty — must prove the ground on the facts; do not import HMA section numbers.

hypotheticals.question: Can HMA s. 13 be cited for an SMA divorce?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Use SMA s. 27 for contested divorce under the Special Marriage Act.

distinctions.title: s. 27 contested vs s. 28 mutual consent
distinctions.right: Joint petition; separation and mutual agreement.

misconceptions.trap: HMA divorce sections apply automatically to SMA marriages.
misconceptions.correction: SMA has its own divorce chapter; cite s. 27 (or s. 28 for mutual consent).
